title: LEAF COLLECTION UNDERWAY
full_story:
The City of Flora Department of Public Works fall curbside leaf collection will begin Sunday, November 1st.  City residents should have their loose leaves to the curbside on their normal scheduled leaf collection day.  Please keep in mind that the crew may run behind schedule during this time, and they appreciate your patience and understanding.  To help crews more efficiently collect leaves, please remember the following, rake leaves in wind rows, a long narrow line, rather than piles next to the curb.  Also, the City will not pick up anything in the alley.

Keep wind rows as close to the curb as possible but do not rake leaves into the street.  This is in violation of a city ordinance and will plug the storm sewers.

Keep wind rows away from trees, hydrants, signposts, electrical pedestals, or other obstacles.

Keep all garbage, metal, branches, and sticks out of the wind rows.

Do not park vehicles next to the leaf wind rows.  If they can’t get the vacuum to the wind rows, they will have to wait until your next collection day.

As a reminder this is a 2-person operation so windrows must be narrow & close to the curb.  Bulky limbs and cuttings from trees and shrubs must be cut into four-foot lengths and tied into bundles not more than two feet in diameter.  Wood and brush should not be placed in a container or garbage can.  Please place this directly on the curb.  All property owners are responsible for disposing of entire trees that are left at the shoulder for collection.  Please work with the City in keeping these guidelines in mind when cleaning up your yard this fall.  If you have any questions, please call the Department of Public Works office at 618-662-4625.

Remember that weather may slow down the leaf picker.  The vacuum will not work if the leaves are extremely wet or if it is snowing.

title: TRICK OR TREAT NIGHTS
full_story:
Villages in Clay County have set their Trick or Treat nights.

Things kick off tomorrow night in Louisville; the Rotary Club and Louisville Community Church’s will have a Trunk or Treat on the square from 6 to 7:30 pm.  The Rotary Club will also be grilling Salt & Strings Butchery Bub Chops and Blair’s Slaughtering & Processing, Inc pork burgers and hot dogs.  Tomorrow night will also be the official Trick or Treat night in Louisville.

In Flora and Clay City Trick or Treat night will be on Thursday from 6 to 8 pm.  The Flora Church of the Nazarene will also have Treats N’ Eats on Thursday, from 6 to 8 pm. They will be serving hot dogs, chips, popcorn, hot chocolate, coffee and water, plus lots of candy for the kids.  Everyone is welcome.

Elsewhere, Noble will have Halloween activities on Friday at the Noble Park, Trick-or-Treat hours for the village will be Saturday from 6 to 8 pm.

The Village of Cisne will host its annual Trunk or Treat and Fall Festival on Friday, in the Cisne Square.  Activities begin at 4:30 pm with trunk or treat, cake walk, costume judging, parade, and bingo.  The parade with feature the Cisne High School and Middle School bands.  Participants are encouraged to decorate their side-by-sides, golf carts, or four-wheelers for the parade lineup on the east side of Key Market.

The Cisne Fire Department will also hold a fundraiser supper Friday evening, beginning at 4 pm at the firehouse.  The menu is chili, peanut-butter sandwiches, desserts, and drinks.  Dine-in and carry-out options will be available.  Cost is by donation and all proceeds will benefit Christmas for Kids in the North Wayne School District.

title: KINMUNDY WOMAN ARRESTED
full_story:
A Kinmundy woman is behind bars following an early morning police chase that stretched from Salem to Iuka.

Salem police say thirty-six-year-old Vanessa Wilkins refused to pull over for a traffic stop on US Route 50 near Lakewood Drive just before three o’clock Monday morning.

Authorities report Wilkins accelerated to high speeds through a residential neighborhood before fleeing eastbound on US Route 50 toward Iuka.

The pursuit came to an unexpected halt when Wilkins’ vehicle developed mechanical problems, slowing to just twenty miles per hour.  She finally pulled into the dollar general parking lot in Iuka, where a Marion County Sheriff’s deputy took her into custody without further incident.

Wilkins was transported to the Marion County jail.  She faces charges of aggravated fleeing and eluding police, aggravated driving on a revoked license, and unlawful possession of a weapon by a felon after deputies reportedly found a switchblade in her possession.

title: ANOTHER COMBINE FIRE
full_story:
Another combine has been lost to flames this one in Marion County.

Emergency crews rushed to rural Alma Sunday afternoon following reports of a heavy field fire.  Kinmundy-Alma Fire Chief Kevin Day reports that when firemen arrived at the Judy Wilkins farm near Oak Grove and Possum Trot Roads, a combine was already completely engulfed in flames.

The crew operating the machine had been harvesting soybeans when the fire broke out around 3 pm.  Quick action by the combine crew managed to knock back the flames enough to prevent the fire from spreading into the unharvested field.

While the machine is considered a total loss, no injuries were reported.  Fire officials say the exact cause of the blaze remains under investigation.

The Xenia Fire Protection District was dispatched Thursday to a combine fire in rural Wayne County.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
The dust continues to fly around Illinois farms as the extended period of abnormally warm and dry conditions provides ample harvest opportunities.  Statewide, 74% of corn and 81% of soybeans were in the bin as of October 25th, both slightly ahead of the average pace, according to the latest USDA crop progress report.  Nationwide, 60% of corn and 79% of soybeans were harvested as of the same date.

According to the USDA there were 6.6 days suitable for field work during the week ending October 25th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 57.7 degrees, 5.3 degrees above normal.  There was no precipitation recorded, 0.76 inches below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 14% very short, 30% short, 52% adequate, and 4% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 15% very short, 30% short, 52% adequate, and 3% surplus.

Corn harvested reached 74%, slightly ahead of the 5-year average of 73%.  Corn condition was rated 3% very poor, 8% poor, 29% fair, 46% good, and 14% excellent.

Soybeans harvested reached 81%, compared to the 5-year average of 77%.

Winter wheat planted reached 70%, compared to the 5-year average of 71%.  Winter wheat emerged reached 40%, compared to the 5-year average of 41%.

title: HALLOWEEN ICASH
full_story:
Ahead of Halloween, Illinois State Treasurer Michael Frerichs is asking residents to check the ICash website to see if there’s missing money waiting for you to claim.

“You might find enough money for a bag of candy, a really good Halloween costume or tickets to a haunted house.  Maybe even enough to take your friends out to see a scary movie,” Frerichs said.  “And speaking of scary movies, I checked the ICash database, and it looks like there’s money waiting for several people named Michael Myers and even a few named Fred Krueger.”

The Treasurer’s Office also found missing money that belongs to a couple of Lizzie Bordens, plenty of Jasons, and several people named Kathy Bates (but no Annie Wilkes).  There is also unclaimed property for some Pumpkins, Ghosts and even a few Gourds.

ICash is one of Illinois’ oldest consumer protection initiatives.  The Illinois State Treasurer’s Office is tasked with safeguarding and returning unclaimed property, including the contents of overlooked safe deposit boxes, unpaid life insurance benefits, forgotten bank accounts and unused rebate cards.  The Illinois Treasurer is legally required to return unclaimed property to its owner or heirs, no matter how long it takes.

Frerichs returned a record $307.8 million in missing money to more than 567,000 residents, businesses and organizations through the ICash program during Fiscal Year 2026.  That broke last year’s mark, when $303.8 million was returned to nearly 312,000 residents.

All told, Frerichs has returned more than $2.65 billion in missing money during his time in office.  When Frerichs first became Treasurer, there were 60,000 claims paid a year.  Today, more than 300,000 claims are paid during a normal year, owing in no small part to Frerichs’ complete restructuring of the missing money process.  The State Treasurer’s Office added electronic claims, eliminated red tape that slowed small-money claims, and even returned money without the need to file a claim.

Frerichs also added a Friends and Family “share” feature.  When visitors to the ICash website come across the name of someone they know, they can select the “share” icon and provide the email address of their friend or relative.  Frerichs’ office will notify the individual by sending an email that mentions the missing money along with the name of the friend or relative who spotted it.  Then, that individual can start the process of retrieving their missing money.

Treasurer Frerichs also has unveiled a Spanish-language missing money website.  The site works the same way as its English-language counterpart.  People enter a name and city or ZIP code into the search box, and if there’s a match, they can start filing a claim online.

Illinois is a national leader in the unclaimed property space and is frequently consulted by other states’ leaders who are seeking to reform their unclaimed property laws, rules, and procedures.

The Illinois State Treasurer’s Office recommends that people check at least twice each year at icash.illinoistreasurer.gov to see if missing money is waiting for you.

title: FEDERAL FUNDING
full_story:
US Representative Mike Bost announced that he has helped secure $34.9 million in federal funding for SUL4R-PLUS Illinois, a sulfur fertilizer manufacturing facility in Marissa to support a nearly $70 million expansion.

“I’m thrilled to see this major investment coming to Marissa,” said Bost.  “Agriculture is the backbone of Southern Illinois’ economy, and investments like this are a win for job growth, manufacturing, and the hardworking farmers who feed and fuel our nation.  Expanding fertilizer production here at home will help reduce our dependence on foreign suppliers and give our farmers greater access to the resources they need to grow and succeed.  I look forward to seeing the positive impact this project will have for years to come.”

The funding, announced by Vice President J.D. Vance and US Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins, is part of the US Department of Agriculture’s Fertilizer Investment & Expansion for Long-Term Domestic Supply (FIELDS) Program.  The investment will help expand domestic fertilizer production, strengthen America’s agricultural supply chain, and reduce reliance on foreign suppliers.

Bost previously authored a letter to the Trump administration urging support for the Marissa project.  It is one of eight fertilizer manufacturing projects selected nationwide through the FIELDS Program, representing more than $1.34 billion in proposed investment, including approximately $573 million in proposed USDA funding.
